one_liner: Source, filter, deduplicate, tokenize, and pack a 20B-token corpus for a 100M-parameter model.

key_terms.definition: Empirical result that training-compute-optimal loss requires parameters N and tokens D scaled together, with D*≈20N; used here to compute the 2B-token compute-optimal baseline.
Deliberately training past the Chinchilla-optimal token budget (here ~200 tok/param, 10x optimal) to shrink N and cut permanent per-query inference cost at a one-time training-compute expense.
The chapter's fixed 20B-token blend: 70% FineWeb-Edu, 15% Cosmopedia v2, 10% StarCoder, 5% FineMath/OpenWebMath, following the SmolLM-style web+synthetic+code+math recipe.

Applying a different heuristic filter per source domain (prose vs. code vs. math) rather than one generic filter, since code/math have character distributions the generic prose filter would wrongly reject.
Hashing each document's normalized text and dropping any repeat, catching verbatim mirrors and copy-pasted boilerplate cheaply in O(1) memory per unique document.

A signature technique that hashes a document's character shingles with many independent hash functions and keeps each function's minimum, so agreement between two signatures unbiasedly estimates Jaccard similarity.

Splitting a MinHash signature into bands of rows and bucketing documents by band; any shared band flags a near-duplicate candidate, turning all-pairs comparison into near-linear lookups governed by an (1/bands)^(1/rows) threshold curve.
Concatenating many short tokenized documents into fixed-length (SEQ_LEN=2048) training windows so no compute is wasted on padding tokens for documents shorter than the context length.
A causal mask that also forbids attention across packed-document boundaries, so a token in one packed document can never attend into another document sharing its training window.
Restarting each document's position ids at 0 when it is packed into a window, so RoPE's relative-position machinery isn't fed positions that falsely continue a preceding, unrelated document.
Storing packed token ids and position ids as 2-byte uint16 arrays in flat binary shard files, memory-mapped at train time so no shard is fully loaded into RAM.
The fraction of a GPU's peak FLOP/s actually sustained during training; used here to sanity-check that the 20B-token budget's 15-25 GPU-hour target is achievable on an A100.
